To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the VEGA and EGEE infrastructures have a number of interoperability problems that make them not interoperable; 2) there exist a number of solutions for the interoperability problems, but they are not implemented in a way that would make them interoperable; 3) the solutions are not compatible with the existing Grid middleware and would require changes in the existing Grid middleware to be implemented; 4) the changes in Grid middleware would require changes in all Grid middleware components, including

(i) the VEGAS Grid middleware can be successfully deployed on EGEE resources, (ii) the VEGAN job submission system can be used for job submission to EGEE resources, and (iii) the VEGANS job submission system can successfully run on the EGEE resources.
the current version of the VEGA Grid infrastructure does not support the creation of Virtual Organizations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions:  1) What are the interoperability issues between the EGEE and VEGAS Grids?
the following questions: How to make Grid infrastructures interoperable?
the following questions: 1) How to provide interoperability among different Grid infrastructures?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interoperability between the two Grid infrastructures is possible but it is not yet fully achieved and it requires a considerable effort from both sides.
the EGEE Grid infrastructure is a very powerful, well designed and reliable system, but its interoperability with other systems is not satisfactory.
there are many interoperability issues between different Grid infrastructures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have successfully demonstrated the possibility to create a Virtual Organization that includes resources from two different Grid infrastructures, namely EGEE and VEGa, and we have also demonstrated the interoperability of two different Grid middleware systems, namely gLite and gLite, and the possibility to create and manage Virtual Organizations using both of them.
we have developed and implemented the necessary components to allow the creation of VO's spanning across different Grid infrastructures.
we have shown that it is possible to build a bridge between two Grid infrastructures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is feasible to build interoperable Grid infrastructures.
the current state of the art is far from interoperability.
the interoperability between different Grid infrastructures is a very difficult task, but not impossible.
